rationales.A: No bills appear; Carnegie sits on bags marked with dollar signs.
rationales.B: The cartoon draws Carnegie reclining on piles of money bags, holding a whip.
rationales.C: No contracts appear; Carnegie sits on bags marked with dollar signs.
rationales.D: No broken machinery appears; Carnegie sits on bags marked with dollar signs.
rationales.general:
Name the object under Carnegie.
1. Carnegie sits on top of a heap of bags.
2. The bags are marked with dollar signs.
3. They are money bags, the cartoonist’s picture of his fortune.
4. So the answer is piles of money bags.
5. Money bags, a whip, and a closed mill are the cartoonist’s whole argument in one picture.
Remember: in a cartoon, labels on objects name what they stand for.

stimulus.text: Political cartoon “Promise and Performance,” published in 1892. A large Andrew Carnegie sits on piles of money bags, holding a whip. Below him stretches a steel mill with signs reading “CLOSED—STRIKE,” “CLOSED,” and “LOCK-OUT.” Crowds of workers stand outside the mill gates.
